subject: Measuring the shift-start checks
mail: So we agreed operators need to learn the 10-minute cleaning and lubrication check at shift start, with a hands-on session and a tablet checklist. My director wants to see it pay off. What do we measure?
snippets: The check: clean, inspect, lubricate, 10 minutes at shift start.
Operators already tick a paper checklist, which is usually fully ticked.
diagnosis: Operators skip or rush the shift-start checks because they were never shown how to do them properly, and dirt and missing lubrication cause many short stops. The agreed fix is hands-on training at the machine plus a time-stamped tablet checklist.

gold.baseline: Unplanned stops caused by dirt, wear or missing lubrication over the last two months, from the machine stop codes.
gold.behaviour: Checks done correctly at shift start, verified by weekly maintenance spot checks at the machine, not by the ticked list.
gold.business_metric: Minutes of unplanned downtime from those causes, per machine, compared with the baseline.
gold.collection: Stop codes from the production system and tablet check logs with time stamps, reviewed monthly by maintenance.

traps: Share of checklists ticked, which is already near 100% on paper.
Overall plant efficiency, which moves with orders and changeovers.
data_available: Production system stop codes per machine, including 'dirt/lubrication'.
Tablet checklist with time stamps (from the new plan).
debrief: A fully ticked paper checklist next to a dirty machine tells you a ticked box is not a behaviour. The strong plan pairs a real check of the behaviour with the specific stops it should prevent, rather than plant-wide efficiency.
